THE ACT IS ITS OWN MUTANT ARM AND THAT IS THE STRONGER READ HERE: phase 1 asserted that all 1,188 stored fields still held exactly the plans' before-values immediately before the write, so the pre-state was measured rather than quoted, and the post-state is the verifier's 1,188 of 1,188 equal to after. The instrument therefore discriminates by construction: the same field was read as before and then as after by two independent programs. ACT (C)'s negative arm is the same shape and adds a CONFIRMED PREDICTION: the pair named SAP_GY's urls_returned None -> 10 BEFORE the GO, derived from the deployed reader's own regex rather than from the input's shape, and the post-act read reproduced exactly that -- one named move, no state move, nothing else. A prediction made from the producer's rule and then confirmed is stronger evidence than an unexpected clean pass.

declared_exclusions.item: The graders print 'plan entries 0 from 0 file(s); stale or unlocatable 0 []' in all three AC runs, and that line is NOT a measurement.
declared_exclusions.reason: The grader's C0 clause is guarded by 'if a.plan:' (b_served_text.py:155-156), so with no --plan it is SKIPPED and emits no PASS or FAIL -- no C0 verdict appears in any of the three outputs, so nothing passed on an empty denominator. --plan is the grader's PRE-ACT path: C0 asserts the served value still equals before and then patches the body in memory so C1-C3 can grade post-act text before the act exists. Run post-act with --plan it would correctly FAIL, because the route now serves after. The TO's literal post-act invocation passes no --plan and is the right one. Recorded because the printed zero reads like a result and a future reader could cite it as if C0 had run.

The PARSED value of those fields is unchanged, which is why CTO condition 3 is graded semantically; the verifier's C3 reads 251 of 251 equal against the base VersionId. A byte-level comparison would have failed here and would have been the wrong instrument, because the condition is about content, not encoding. ak6_store_writes.json records prior_nonascii per key so the change is visible rather than silent.
